introduction: Learn how Formula 1 cars use airflow, wings and aerodynamic surfaces to generate downforce while managing drag.

interactiveConcepts.title: Airflow Around the Car
interactiveConcepts.description: Explore how airflow interacts with the car's aerodynamic surfaces.

interactiveConcepts.title: Front and Rear Wing Effects
interactiveConcepts.description: Explore how the front and rear wings influence aerodynamic performance.

interactiveConcepts.title: Aerodynamic Balance

glossary.definition: Aerodynamic force that pushes the car toward the track and increases tyre load.
Aerodynamic resistance that opposes the car's movement through the air.
The distribution of aerodynamic load between the front and rear of the car.
The movement of air around and through the aerodynamic surfaces of the car.

testYourself.question: What is the main purpose of aerodynamic downforce?
options: To push the car toward the track
testYourself.explanation: Downforce pushes the car toward the track, increasing the load on the tyres and helping the car generate grip through corners.

testYourself.question: What is aerodynamic drag?
options: A force that opposes the car's motion through the air
The force that turns the steering wheel
The force produced by the brakes
testYourself.explanation: Drag is aerodynamic resistance that acts against the car's movement through the air. Reducing drag can help improve straight-line speed.

testYourself.question: Why is aerodynamic balance important?
options: It determines the driver's helmet size
It helps distribute aerodynamic load between the front and rear
testYourself.explanation: Aerodynamic balance describes how aerodynamic load is distributed between the front and rear of the car. A suitable balance helps the car remain predictable and stable.
